summary: Organised local opposition emerged quickly after the February 2026 EIA scoping submission. A Change.org petition launched 4 June 2026 had ~3,150 signatures by late July 2026; APRS is campaigning against the scheme and publicised a 'Defend your Castle' protest at a Clan Hunter gathering aimed at the Hunterston Estate as landowner; Scottish Greens MSP Cara McKee has called for a national moratorium on hyperscale data centres pending Scottish Government guidance. No application is yet open for formal representations.

principal_concerns.concern: Loss of ~88 ha (petition says ~84 ha, APRS 'almost 200 acres') of agricultural land, woodland, wetland and watercourses; industrialisation of open countryside in an area already hosting Clydeport, the ore terminal and coal yard
Harm to the setting of Hunterston Castle, Hunterston House and Portencross Castle, and to buried archaeology in an area of high archaeological potential
principal_concerns.raised_by: West of Scotland Archaeology Service (scoping response); petition signatories

principal_concerns.concern: A78 traffic congestion through Seamill and Fairlie, and unsafe site access — historic stone pillars at the South Entrance too narrow for two-way HGV traffic
Water and power consumption of hyperscale data centres, and potential impacts on the Firth of Clyde marine environment, seabirds and marine mammals
principal_concerns.raised_by: Cara McKee MSP (Scottish Greens); petition signatories

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Investment exceeding £10bn, described as one of the largest private investments in Ayrshire's history, with 1,000+ construction jobs

stakeholder_positions.position: Called for a halt to all hyperscale data centre developments (including Hunterston) until a national strategy and guidance for councils is in place, citing water, power and energy-price concerns.
Confirmed no formal planning application is under consideration; any future proposal would undergo robust statutory assessment including full EIA.

Scoping approach 'generally satisfactory' but site has high archaeological potential; recommends non-invasive survey and trial trenching before determination and protection of historic landscape links to Hunterston House and Castle.

planning_authority_contact: North Ayrshire Council planning (case officer for scoping: Iain Davies)
notes: Fairlie Community Council is the community council for the site per the portal record; its formal position has not been located. Petition figures are self-reported by Change.org and change over time.
